newsitem.title: UK: "Pocket Budget" - summary issued by UK Treasury 3.
newsitem.headline: "Pocket Budget" - summary issued by UK Treasury 3.

text.p: The overall effect of the tax measures in this Budget is to reduce Government borrowing this year and next. Taken together they will help create a stronger and fairer society and equip Britain for our long-term future. The Budget addresses Britain's failure to invest in the long term. It will release resources for hospitals and schools and help the economy grow.
The economy is expected to grow by 3 per cent in 1997 and 2 per cent in 1998.
Underlying inflation is forecast to remain at around 2 per cent in 1997 and to rise slightly to 2 per cent in 1998.
Unemployment remains high - 2.1 million according to the Labour Force Survey. Youth and long-term unemployment are serious concerns.

Excluding the temporary effects of the windfall tax and spending on Welfare to Work, the Public Sector Borrowing Requirement is forecast to be 13 billion in 1997-98 and 5 billion in 1998-99(11 billion and 4 billion including the windfall tax and associated spending).
Consumer spending is forecast to increase by 4 per cent in 1997 and 4 per cent in 1998.
Total investment by businesses is forecast to rise by 9 per cent in 1997 and 6 per cent in 1998.

-- Encouraging long-term investment -- - corporation tax cut from 33% to 31% - small companies' corporation tax cut from 23% to 21% - tax credit arrangements reformed to encourage companies to retain and reinvest profits - capital allowances doubled to 50% on plant and machinery for small- and medium-sized businesses(for one year only) - local authority receipts --900 million released for new housing

-5.2 billion Welfare to Work package, financed by the windfall tax on the excess profits of privatised utilities, for young and long-term unemployed and lone parents. Includes 1.3 billion for school buildings and equipment
-Schools: an extra 1 billion for local authorities to spend next year (plus 1.3 billion from windfall tax)
-National Health Service: an extra 1.2 billion next year
Moving towards a fairer tax system
-VAT on domestic fuel and power cut from 8% to 5%
-private medical insurance: tax relief abolished for over-60s
-anti-avoidance package: ensuring everyone pays the proper amount
- duty on petrol and diesel increased immediately by 6% more than inflation tobacco duties increased from December by 5% more than inflation
- vehicle excise duty increased from November - reductions for "clean" buses and lorries to follow.
